accepted_scope_caveats.label: Theorem: identification frontier / ass:latent-profile-plane
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The iff frontier is conditional on the unobserved low-rank latent cumulant-profile restriction and on the deliberately source-labelled domain D_rho; it is not an identification claim for arbitrary simultaneous shifts.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Exact identification versus source-label ambiguity UNDER the maintained calibrated latent-profile-plane model.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: Theorem: weak-breakout frontier
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The minimax spine remains conditional on constructing the stated full-observation same-shell lower-bound family; the generated-projector limit theory is expressly left open.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Rate-optimality UNDER the bounded-moment, fixed-gap shell model once its density-level lower-bound construction is established.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 2228–2229, §3.6 Theorem 3.6 and source-swap proof; p. 2231, §6 Conclusion
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Theorem 3.6 proves nonidentification with two environments when both treatment and latent exogenous noises vary, using the displayed source swap; the conclusion explicitly names more-than-two-environment generalization as future work.
BACKSHIFT gives the pairwise intervention-variance nonproportionality condition for unique joint diagonalization and states that at least three environments are required.
Theorem 3.1 equates the Generalized Causal Dantzig GMM zero set with the environmental Causal Dantzig invariance constraints.

SR-AR and SR-CQLR are introduced for supplied linear and nonlinear moment conditions with uniform asymptotic size under weak conditions and without restrictions on the expected Jacobian or variance-matrix eigenvalues.

The article studies multiple-context linear causal disentanglement, derives coupled higher-cumulant tensor recovery under perfect latent interventions, and characterizes a soft-intervention equivalence class.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Replace the informal Sachs motivation with an observable diagnostic or a generative shared-factor condition that implies the latent-profile-plane restriction, then report when the diagnostic supports the maintained regime.
Make the weak-breakout theorem depend on an explicit positive full-law local family and prove its KL bound, rather than leaving that construction only in the technical limitation.

Add a generic-class result showing precisely when every two-environment marginal remains source-ambiguous while the joint E-environment law breaks ambiguity; this would sharpen the contrast with Kivva et al. beyond the conditional frontier.

recommended_next_step: Advance the conditional field-tier identification kernel to Stage 0, prioritizing the legal delayed-order witness and the full-law weak-breakout lower-bound construction.
